newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India slides as locals lose five pct.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India slides as locals lose five pct.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) slid in London trade, but failed to keep pace with losses on the local market, having also sat out much of the rally among domestic stocks this week.
"No one knows where India is going and the GDR market has not been as enthusiastic as the locals in pushing higher," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 1.29 points, 1.82 percent, at 69.35 points, with the premium over the local market at 14.86 percent compared with yesterday's 10.74 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 190.85 points, 5.23 percent, to 3455.88.

"I think everyone knew the rate Bombay was rising was unsustainable, but where we go from here is another matter. The government is clearly going to try to support the market with major issues such as VSNL due. I suspect the locals will open firm tomorrow," said a trader.
Investors are also waiting for an announcement on capital market reforms, which had been delayed since mid-January.
"This market has risen early this year on a lot of expecations and hopes, only today we had news on infrastructure project improvements," said a trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 0.74 points, 1.06 percent, to 70.05, a premium of 47.94 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index gained 12.10 points 1.73 percent to 711.86.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 0.26 points to 97.25, a premium of 5.85 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index gained 40.96 points, 0.57 percent, to close at 7,206.42.
